## Overview

Add an opt-in XPU compile pass that fuses routed experts and one sigmoid-gated shared expert for Qwen MoE decode. Support FP16/BF16 activations with online/static per-tensor FP8 weights while preserving the existing gate/top-k routing and tensor-parallel reduction.

Companion kernels: [vllm-xpu-kernels#637](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-xpu-kernels/pull/637), derived from [#628](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-xpu-kernels/pull/628). Router/norm extensions from [kernel #629](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-xpu-kernels/pull/629) are not required.

## Claims

- Replace the shared/routed tuple and its unscaled addition with one XPU custom op for supported decode ranges, with FP16/BF16 activations and online/static per-tensor FP8 weights. Default is off: `pass_config.fuse_xpu_moe_shared`; eligible compile ranges end at or below `pass_config.xpu_moe_shared_fusion_max_token_num` (default 8 tokens).
- Preserve the existing router and TP reduction. No model, scheduler, worker or common MoE implementation changes.
- Include the pass/adapter source and native operator schema/availability in the enabled pass's cache hash, and initialize per-layer plans lazily so AOT-loaded graphs use the correct runtime state.
- B1 TPOT drops by 20.2% (FP16) / 20.7% (BF16) with graph, and 45.7% / 44.8% with compile but no graph. Other batches/modes, including regressions, are shown below; eager does not dispatch this pass.

## Validation

**Current review validation.** vLLM `56e3af32a9ef48dea67837ffe12468fefa950ca1` with kernels `bf86b379dff1cf9782d6dd09a1fedf32580fa910`: **210 native tests**, **61 vLLM pass/adapter/configuration tests**, and changed-file pre-commit checks passed. The installed native library hashes and worker mappings were checked. The int64 regression fails on the pre-fix library and passes on this revision; its trigger is an out-of-range expert ID, not a newly observed normal-Qwen accuracy failure.

The latest FP16 TP2 B1 graph-on smoke (32,768 input / 256 output, one warmup and three measured runs) reports a median TPOT of **7.777 ms/token** and **GSM8K20 19/20**, with no output truncation. Both ranks create 40 fused plans and capture token counts 1/2/4/8. This smoke uses temperature 0, seed 0, five-shot GSM8K and a 2,048-token cap. It is separate from the historical paired measurements below; it does not establish a new before/after speedup. The latest whole-model smoke covers FP16 only; native tests cover both FP16 and BF16.

The additional **compile, graph off** smoke at the same current revisions and FP16 TP2 B1 configuration uses `mode=3`, `cudagraph_mode=NONE`, and `fuse_xpu_moe_shared=true`. One warmup (25.862 ms/token) was followed by three measured TPOT values: 25.670, 25.609, 25.614 ms/token; median **25.614 ms/token**, median end-to-end output throughput **37.92 tok/s**. GSM8K20 scored **19/20**, without truncated or invalid answers. Both ranks instantiated 40 fused plans and recorded no graph captures. This is a current-revision smoke check, not a new paired baseline comparison.

**Historical paired measurements.** The tables below retain the original E2E, native and AOT measurements at vLLM `8d6276269b212ccfbd472d3cde99e3122456025b` (official main base `187a0eb98aa42341d703f83421d693fa7585581b`) and kernels `f1094da6a236229a50146d01ab9ebc7d620d68e7` (official main base `78799feacc02fd2fd52fe01b847ae5ae681b9627`). The full FP16/BF16 B1/2/4/8 matrix and cold/hot AOT comparisons have not been repeated for the latest review revision. The current vLLM change is based on official main `bfa7e5b7afe40ebe48288801a2baf5c1135cd881`.

Hardware: Intel Arc Pro B70 (Xe2), TP2, Qwen3.6-35B-A3B, online FP8 weights, FP16/BF16 activations. Environment: `vllm/vllm-openai-xpu:v0.31.0` as the base image, with torch `2.14.0+xpu` and vLLM/kernel source builds. The image tag describes the environment; the source revisions above identify the tested implementation.

- Pass, adapter, numeric and configuration tests: **61 passed**; targeted pre-commit checks and mypy pass.
- Companion native numerical/negative/replay tests: **74 passed**, including changed inputs/routing on a non-default XPU stream through XPUGraph replay.
- Both TP ranks instantiate 40 fused MoE plans in each enabled compile case; disabled/eager cases instantiate zero. Cold compile logs/FX snapshots verify 40 rewrites per rank, and capture descriptors record the actual graph shapes.
- FP16 and BF16 warm restarts, with `VLLM_FORCE_AOT_LOAD=1`, directly load the AOT artifact on both ranks, create 40 fresh lazy plans per rank, and exactly match all four cold-run greedy responses.

| Activation | Mode | B1 TPOT (ms) | B2 | B4 | B8 |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| float16 | Eager: no fusion dispatch | 46.580 → 46.845 | 45.190 → 46.745 | 46.675 → 46.890 | 46.365 → 47.280 |
| float16 | Compile, graph off | 47.630 → 25.860 (+45.7%) | 47.610 → 25.810 (+45.8%) | 47.835 → 26.075 (+45.5%) | 47.995 → 26.480 (+44.8%) |
| float16 | Compile + graph | 9.605 → 7.665 (+20.2%) | 11.830 → 10.135 (+14.3%) | 14.365 → 13.040 (+9.2%) | 19.815 → 18.955 (+4.3%) |
| bfloat16 | Eager: no fusion dispatch | 46.635 → 46.230 | 46.230 → 46.410 | 46.715 → 46.450 | 47.235 → 47.065 |
| bfloat16 | Compile, graph off | 46.990 → 25.920 (+44.8%) | 47.210 → 26.310 (+44.3%) | 47.410 → 26.035 (+45.1%) | 47.215 → 26.155 (+44.6%) |
| bfloat16 | Compile + graph | 9.740 → 7.725 (+20.7%) | 11.715 → 9.895 (+15.5%) | 14.775 → 13.210 (+10.6%) | 20.015 → 19.195 (+4.1%) |

<details>
<summary>Hot-run ranges (runs 2–3)</summary>

| Activation | Mode | B1 hot range (ms) | B2 | B4 | B8 |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| float16 | eager | 46.42–46.74 → 46.69–47.00 | 45.07–45.31 → 46.65–46.84 | 46.49–46.86 → 46.87–46.91 | 46.36–46.37 → 47.15–47.41 |
| float16 | off | 47.25–48.01 → 25.65–26.07 | 47.50–47.72 → 25.75–25.87 | 47.83–47.84 → 26.01–26.14 | 47.48–48.51 → 26.43–26.53 |
| float16 | on | 9.60–9.61 → 7.66–7.67 | 11.83–11.83 → 10.13–10.14 | 14.36–14.37 → 13.04–13.04 | 19.81–19.82 → 18.80–19.11 |
| bfloat16 | eager | 46.23–47.04 → 46.11–46.35 | 46.21–46.25 → 46.40–46.42 | 46.60–46.83 → 46.34–46.56 | 47.21–47.26 → 47.01–47.12 |
| bfloat16 | off | 46.83–47.15 → 25.81–26.03 | 46.99–47.43 → 26.30–26.32 | 47.35–47.47 → 26.03–26.04 | 46.97–47.46 → 26.14–26.17 |
| bfloat16 | on | 9.74–9.74 → 7.72–7.73 | 11.71–11.72 → 9.89–9.90 | 14.77–14.78 → 13.21–13.21 | 20.00–20.03 → 19.19–19.20 |

</details>

32,768 input tokens / 256 generated tokens, `ignore_eos`, random dataset seed 0, B1/2/4/8. Three runs per batch; report the median of runs 2–3 and retain the full range. Prefix caching enabled, `max_model_len=40960`, `max_num_seqs=8`, `max_num_batched_tokens=1024`, GPU memory utilization 0.90, block size 64, OMP threads 32. Both arms use the same native libraries and only change the pass flag.

| Activation | Mode | Baseline GSM8K20 | Flag on |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: |
| float16 | eager | 19/20 | 19/20 |
| float16 | on | 19/20 | 19/20 |
| bfloat16 | eager | 19/20 | 19/20 |
| bfloat16 | on | 19/20 | 19/20 |

GSM8K smoke evaluation uses the first 20 test questions, five training examples, chat endpoint, temperature 1, seed 42 and a 5,120-token limit. These small evaluations do not establish a full-dataset accuracy result. Greedy output comparison: float16_eager: 4/4 exact; float16_off: 2/4 exact; float16_on: 2/4 exact; bfloat16_eager: 4/4 exact; bfloat16_off: 2/4 exact; bfloat16_on: 2/4 exact. Differences from the unfused path are evaluated alongside independent kernel numerics and GSM8K; they are not treated as bitwise equivalence.

Reproduce the serving comparison in an XPU virtualenv. Set the checkpoint path, select two available devices with `ZE_AFFINITY_MASK`, and choose `float16` / `bfloat16`:

```bash
OMP_NUM_THREADS=32 \
  .venv/bin/python -m vllm.entrypoints.openai.api_server \
  --model /path/to/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B \
  --served-model-name Qwen3.6-35B-A3B --dtype float16 --quantization fp8 \
  --tensor-parallel-size 2 --host 127.0.0.1 --port 18467 \
  --reasoning-parser qwen3 --attention-backend FLASH_ATTN \
  --max-model-len 40960 --max-num-seqs 8 --max-num-batched-tokens 1024 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.90 --block-size 64 \
  --compilation-config '{"mode":3,"backend":"inductor","splitting_ops":[],"cudagraph_mode":"FULL_DECODE_ONLY","cudagraph_capture_sizes":[1,2,4,8],"compile_ranges_endpoints":[8],"pass_config":{"fuse_xpu_moe_shared":true}}'

# Run each batch three times; change 1 to 2, 4 or 8.
.venv/bin/python -m vllm.entrypoints.cli.main bench serve \
  --model /path/to/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B \
  --served-model-name Qwen3.6-35B-A3B --port 18467 \
  --dataset-name random --seed 0 --temperature 0 --ignore-eos \
  --random-input-len 32768 --random-output-len 256 --num-prompts 1

.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q \
  tests/compile/passes/test_xpu_fusion.py tests/compile/test_config.py \
  -k 'xpu_moe or xpu_fusion'
```

Set the pass flag to `false` for the baseline; set `cudagraph_mode` to `NONE` for compile without graph. For actual eager use `--enforce-eager`: the compile pass does not execute, including when requested, and eager timing differences are not fusion gains.

## Details

This is the standalone MoE integration extracted from Wang Yuchen's broader [#60539](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/60539): MoE commit `5246fc07e`, consolidated AMD-style pass organization `53f6b044e`, online FP8 support `8f3e461be`, and BF16 support `fc84b8304`. It uses the independent operator API from [kernel #628](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-xpu-kernels/pull/628), with review fixes in companion [#637](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-xpu-kernels/pull/637). The router/norm extensions of [#629](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-xpu-kernels/pull/629) are not required. Additional safeguards require distinct single-use tuple outputs, rank-two contiguous input and `aten.add` with `alpha=1`; the AOT cache also tracks the relevant source and native schema. The source relationship is explicit so this MoE split can be coordinated with the original upstream PR.

Scope is AR decode: no [kernel #629](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-xpu-kernels/pull/629) router kernel, norm/QKV/projection fusion, standalone GEMM/GEMV optimization, in-place all-reduce, GDN output allocation change or speculative/MTP warmup patch. The current pass targets hidden size 2048, 256 experts, top-k 8 and matching routed/shared intermediate sizes on Xe2/Xe3. Kernel support is queried through the companion package's `supports()` helper, which requires positive H/I multiples of 32. The targeted H=2048 and I=256/512 satisfy that contract. Unsupported dimensions keep the original graph; native entry checks additionally enforce tensor/device/alignment/workspace requirements before submission. FP8 block scaling, LoRA, EP/EPLB, DP/PCP/SP and other unsupported layer configurations keep the original graph. The sizeable XPU implementation is isolated from common inference paths and justified by the measured E2E comparison above.

User-facing configuration is documented in `docs/design/fusions.md`, with an entry from the Intel XPU installation page: eager behavior, compile without graph, compile with graph and the supported token range. Existing compilation-pass CI collects graph/config tests; native XPU and checkpoint E2E coverage is provided by the hardware validation above, since generic non-XPU CI cannot exercise that path.

Scope is AR decode: no [kernel #629](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-xpu-kernels/pull/629) router kernel, norm/QKV/projection fusion, standalone GEMM/GEMV optimization, in-place all-reduce, GDN output allocation change or speculative/MTP warmup patch. The current pass targets hidden size 2048, 256 experts, top-k 8 and matching routed/shared intermediate sizes on Xe2/Xe3. Kernel support is queried through the companion package's `supports()` helper, which requires positive H/I multiples of 32. The targeted H=2048 and I=256/512 satisfy that contract. Unsupported dimensions keep the original graph; native entry checks additionally enforce tensor/device/alignment/workspace requirements before submission. FP8 block scaling, LoRA, EP/EPLB, DP/PCP/SP and other unsupported layer configurations keep the original graph. The sizeable XPU implementation is isolated from common inference paths and justified by the measured E2E comparison above.

User-facing configuration is documented in `docs/design/fusions.md`, with an entry from the Intel XPU installation page: eager behavior, compile without graph, compile with graph and the supported token range. Existing compilation-pass CI collects graph/config tests; native XPU and checkpoint E2E coverage is provided by the hardware validation above, since generic non-XPU CI cannot exercise that path.

+### XPU MoE + Shared Expert (`fuse_xpu_moe_shared`)
+
+**What it fuses.** Combines the routed experts and one sigmoid-gated shared
+expert into one custom op: gate-up projections, SiLU-and-mul, down projections,
+routing-weight combine and the gated shared output. The op submits six kernels;
+router/top-k selection and the tensor-parallel all-reduce remain outside it.
+
+**Requirements.** Intel Xe2/Xe3 and a `vllm-xpu-kernels` build providing
+`_xpu_C.moe_shared_fused_decode_interface`. Activations must be FP16 or BF16;
+routed and shared weights must be FP8 E4M3 with per-tensor FP32 scales
+(one scale per routed expert and one per shared projection).
+The current pass targets Qwen MoE configurations with hidden size 2048,
+256 experts, top-k 8, and matching routed/shared intermediate sizes, using
+SiLU without bias. It was validated on Qwen3.6-35B-A3B with TP2.
+LoRA, expert parallelism, EPLB, data parallelism, prefill context parallelism,
+sequence parallelism, zero-expert routing and microbatching (DBO or a fixed
+`ubatch_size` > 1) are not supported by this pass.
+
+**Default and token range.** Disabled at every optimization level unless
+`pass_config.fuse_xpu_moe_shared=true`. The pass applies only to compile ranges
+ending at or below `pass_config.xpu_moe_shared_fusion_max_token_num`
+(default: 8 tokens; supported setting: 1–64). Larger ranges keep the original
+MoE path. If the native op is unavailable, a MoE layer is unsupported, or the
+graph pattern does not match, the original operations are kept.
+
+**Compile without graph.** This enables the fusion through vLLM's Inductor
+pipeline, while disabling graph capture/replay:
+
+```bash
+vllm serve /path/to/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B \
+    --tensor-parallel-size 2 --dtype bfloat16 --quantization fp8 \
+    --max-num-seqs 8 \
+    --compilation-config '{
+        "mode": 3,
+        "backend": "inductor",
+        "splitting_ops": [],
+        "cudagraph_mode": "NONE",
+        "compile_ranges_endpoints": [8],
+        "pass_config": {"fuse_xpu_moe_shared": true}
+    }'
+```
+
+**Compile with graph.** Use the same compile setup with decode-only graph
+capture for token counts 1, 2, 4 and 8:
+
+```bash
+vllm serve /path/to/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B \
+    --tensor-parallel-size 2 --dtype bfloat16 --quantization fp8 \
+    --max-num-seqs 8 \
+    --compilation-config '{
+        "mode": 3,
+        "backend": "inductor",
+        "splitting_ops": [],
+        "cudagraph_mode": "FULL_DECODE_ONLY",
+        "cudagraph_capture_sizes": [1, 2, 4, 8],
+        "compile_ranges_endpoints": [8],
+        "pass_config": {"fuse_xpu_moe_shared": true}
+    }'
+```

+The `cudagraph_mode` field controls XPU graphs on Intel GPUs. Use
+`--dtype float16` for FP16 activations, or set `fuse_xpu_moe_shared` to `false`
+for an unfused baseline with the same compile/graph settings.

+**Eager mode.** `--enforce-eager` disables both compilation and graph replay,

+`--enforce-eager` when using either compile configuration above.

+import contextlib

+from typing import Any

+from torch import fx

+from vllm.compilation.passes.fusion.xpu_fusion import (

+from vllm.model_executor.layers.fused_moe.activation import MoEActivation
+from vllm.model_executor.layers.fused_moe.experts.xpu_moe import XPUExpertsFp8

+# Schema of the op as registered by vllm._xpu_ops (torch >= 2.11: LayerName).
+FUSED_SCHEMA = (
+    "vllm::xpu_moe_shared_fused(Tensor hidden_states, Tensor router_logits, "
+    "{layer_name_type} layer_name) -> Tensor"

+

+def _xpu_ops_or_skip():
+    pytest.importorskip("vllm_xpu_kernels")
+    import vllm._xpu_ops as xpu_ops_mod
+
+    return xpu_ops_mod

+
+def _fused_target():
+    """The rewrite target; registered by vllm._xpu_ops on XPU, or a stand-in
+    op with the same signature where that module cannot be imported."""
+    if not hasattr(torch.ops.vllm, "xpu_moe_shared_fused"):
+        from vllm.utils.torch_utils import LayerNameType, direct_register_custom_op
+
+        def _impl(
+            hidden_states: torch.Tensor,
+            router_logits: torch.Tensor,
+            layer_name: LayerNameType,
+        ) -> torch.Tensor:
+            return torch.empty_like(hidden_states)
+
+        direct_register_custom_op(
+            op_name="xpu_moe_shared_fused", op_func=_impl, fake_impl=_impl
+        )
+    return torch.ops.vllm.xpu_moe_shared_fused.default
+
+
+# Use the real registration when vllm._xpu_ops is importable.
+with contextlib.suppress(ImportError):
+    import vllm._xpu_ops  # noqa: F401
+FUSED = _fused_target()
+
+
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+# (a) graph rewrite
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+def _moe_layer(g, x, layer, *, router_in=None, input_ids=None):
+    moe = g.call_function(
+        MOE, (x, x if router_in is None else router_in, x, input_ids, layer, 0)
+    )
+    shared = g.call_function(operator.getitem, (moe, 0))
+    routed = g.call_function(operator.getitem, (moe, 1))
+    add = g.call_function(torch.ops.aten.add.Tensor, (shared, routed))
+    add.meta["val"] = x.meta["val"]
+    out = g.call_function(torch.ops.aten.mul.Tensor, (add, 2.0))
+    out.meta["val"] = x.meta["val"]
+    return moe, shared, routed, add, out
+
+
+def _graph(num_layers=2, dtype=torch.float16, **kw):
+    g = fx.Graph()
+    x = g.placeholder("x")
+    x.meta["val"] = torch.empty(4, HIDDEN, dtype=dtype, device="meta")
+    extra = []
+    for i in range(num_layers):
+        layer = g.placeholder(f"layer_{i}")
+        nodes = _moe_layer(g, x, layer, **kw)
+        extra.append(nodes)
+        x = nodes[-1]
+    g.output(x)
+    return g, extra
+
+
+def _count(g, target):

+                and spec.weight == kFp8StaticTensorSym
+                and spec.activation is None
+                for spec in (args.linear, args.moe)
+            )

+        return False

+
+def _xpu_moe_shared_fused_available() -> bool:
+    # vllm._xpu_ops needs vllm_xpu_kernels; treat an import failure as "not
+    # available" so compilation never fails because of this pass.
+    try:
+        from vllm._xpu_ops import xpu_moe_shared_fused_available
+    except ImportError:
+        return False
+    return xpu_moe_shared_fused_available()
+
+
+class XpuMoESharedFusionPass(VllmInductorPass):
+    """Replace routed + shared MoE with one fused XPU op for small token counts.
+
+    Matches, per MoE layer::
+
+        out = vllm.moe_forward_shared(hidden, hidden, hidden, None, layer, 0)
+        shared, routed = out[0], out[1]
+        y = shared + routed
+
+    and rewrites it to ``y = vllm.xpu_moe_shared_fused(hidden, hidden, layer)``.
+    The TP all-reduce consuming ``y`` is kept. Only applied for compile ranges
+    whose end is <= ``pass_config.xpu_moe_shared_fusion_max_token_num``, and only
+    when every MoE layer of the model supports the fused op; anything that does
+    not match the pattern is left unchanged.
+    """
+
+    def __init__(self, config: VllmConfig):
+        super().__init__(config)
+
+        pass_config = config.compilation_config.pass_config
+        self.max_token_num = pass_config.xpu_moe_shared_fusion_max_token_num
+        mc = config.model_config
+        hf = mc.hf_text_config if mc is not None else None
+        pc = config.parallel_config
+        self.enabled = (
+            hf is not None
+            and mc.dtype in (torch.float16, torch.bfloat16)
+            and getattr(hf, "hidden_size", None) == 2048
+            and getattr(hf, "num_experts", None) == 256
+            and getattr(hf, "num_experts_per_tok", None) == 8
+            and getattr(hf, "shared_expert_intermediate_size", 0) > 0
+            and _is_fp8_per_tensor(config)
+            and config.lora_config is None
+            and not pc.enable_expert_parallel
+            and not pc.enable_eplb
+            and not pc.use_ubatching
+            and _xpu_moe_shared_fused_available()
+        )
+        if not self.enabled:
+            logger.warning_once(
+                "XpuMoESharedFusionPass disabled: model, quantization, parallel "
+                "config or kernel not supported."
+            )
+        else:
+            self.enabled = self._all_moe_layers_supported(config)
+        self.matched_count = 0
+
+    @staticmethod
+    def _all_moe_layers_supported(config: VllmConfig) -> bool:
+        from vllm._xpu_ops import xpu_moe_shared_fused_unsupported_reason
+        from vllm.model_executor.layers.fused_moe.runner.moe_runner import MoERunner
+
+        runners = get_layers_from_vllm_config(config, MoERunner)
+        if not runners:
+            logger.warning_once("XpuMoESharedFusionPass disabled: no MoE layers.")
+            return False
+        for name, runner in runners.items():
+            reason = xpu_moe_shared_fused_unsupported_reason(runner)
+            if reason is not None:
+                logger.warning_once(
+                    "XpuMoESharedFusionPass disabled: MoE layer %s is not "
+                    "supported (%s).",
+                    name,
+                    reason,
+                )
+                return False
+        return True
+
+    def is_applicable_for_range(self, compile_range: Range) -> bool:
+        return self.enabled and compile_range.end <= self.max_token_num
+
+    @staticmethod
+    def _match(node: fx.Node) -> tuple[fx.Node | None, str]:
+        """Return the `add` node combining shared and routed outputs."""
+        if len(node.args) != 6 or len(node.users) != 2:
+            return None, "unsupported arguments or extra output consumers"
+        hidden, router_in, shared_in, input_ids, _layer, unpadded = node.args
+        if router_in is not hidden:
+            return None, "router input is not the hidden states"
+        if shared_in is not hidden or input_ids is not None or unpadded != 0:
+            return None, "unsupported moe_forward_shared arguments"
+        getitems = {}
+        for user in node.users:
+            if (
+                user.target is not operator.getitem
+                or len(user.args) != 2
+                or user.args[1] not in (0, 1)
+                or user.args[1] in getitems
+                or len(user.users) != 1
+            ):
+                return None, "unexpected users of moe_forward_shared"
+            getitems[user.args[1]] = user
+        if set(getitems) != {0, 1}:
+            return None, "unexpected users of moe_forward_shared"
+        add = next(iter(getitems[0].users))
+        if (
+            add is not next(iter(getitems[1].users))
+            or add.target is not torch.ops.aten.add.Tensor
+            or len(add.args) != 2
+            or add.kwargs.get("alpha", 1) != 1
+            or set(add.args) != {getitems[0], getitems[1]}
+        ):
+            return None, "shared and routed outputs are not simply added"
+        val = hidden.meta.get("val")
+        if (
+            not isinstance(val, torch.Tensor)
+            or val.ndim != 2
+            or not val.is_contiguous()
+            or val.dtype not in (torch.float16, torch.bfloat16)
+            or val.shape[-1] != 2048
+        ):
+            return None, "unsupported hidden states dtype/shape"
+        return add, ""
+
+    @VllmInductorPass.time_and_log
+    def __call__(self, graph: fx.Graph) -> None:
+        self.matched_count = 0
+        skipped = 0
+        target = torch.ops.vllm.moe_forward_shared.default
+        for node in list(graph.nodes):
+            if node.op != "call_function" or node.target is not target:
+                continue
+            add, reason = self._match(node)
+            if add is None:
+                logger.debug("XpuMoESharedFusionPass skipped %s: %s", node, reason)
+                skipped += 1
+                continue
+            hidden, router_in, _, _, layer_name = node.args[:5]
+            with graph.inserting_before(add):
+                fused = graph.call_function(
+                    torch.ops.vllm.xpu_moe_shared_fused.default,
+                    (hidden, router_in, layer_name),
+                )
+            fused.meta["val"] = add.meta["val"]
+            add.replace_all_uses_with(fused)
+            getitems = list(node.users)
+            graph.erase_node(add)
+            for g in getitems:
+                graph.erase_node(g)
+            graph.erase_node(node)
+            self.matched_count += 1
+        logger.info(
+            "XpuMoESharedFusionPass replaced %d MoE layers (%d not matched)",
+            self.matched_count,
+            skipped,
+        )
+
+    def uuid(self) -> str:
+        return self.hash_source(self) + f"|{self.enabled}|{self.max_token_num}"
